title: Venturi Effect: Throat Velocity Increase and Pressure Drop
pedagogical_goal: Demonstrate how fluid velocity increases and pressure decreases in a constricted pipe section (Venturi throat) due to conservation of mass and energy, enabling flow rate measurement via pressure differential.

fundamental_laws: Continuity Equation: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ (mass conservation for incompressible flow)
Bernoulli's Equation: P₁ + ½ρv₁² + ρgh₁ = P₂ + ½ρv₂² + ρgh₂ (energy conservation along a streamline, neglecting height change)
Pressure Drop: ΔP = P₁ - P₂ = ½ρ(v₂² - v₁²)

components.description: A smooth Venturi tube geometry: converging section from inlet to throat, then diverging section back to outlet. Path defined as: M 50,240 Q 150,80 250,240 T 450,240 (symmetric inlet-throat-outlet). Stroke: #38bdf8, stroke-width: 4, fill: none.

Five evenly spaced streamlines flowing left to right. Each streamline is a cubic Bezier curve that compresses vertically in the throat region to visualize velocity increase. Start points: (50, y) for y in [120, 160, 200, 240, 280]; End points: (910, y). Control points adjust based on local tube height to show streamline convergence.

A vertical pressure gradient bar on the left side (x=20) showing pressure distribution. Height mapped from inlet pressure (top) to throat pressure (bottom) using a linear gradient fill from #f43f5e (high pressure) to #38bdf8 (low pressure). Width: 20px. Height: 200px, positioned at y=140.

Three pairs of velocity vector arrows (inlet, throat, outlet) showing magnitude and direction. Each pair consists of a line and an arrowhead (polyline). Inlet: short vectors (low velocity), throat: long vectors (high velocity), outlet: medium vectors. Color: #34d399. Animated to pulse with flow.

Two vertical manometer tubes connected to inlet and throat pressure taps. Fluid columns (rectangles) rise to heights proportional to local pressure. Inlet column taller (high pressure), throat column shorter (low pressure). Fluid color: #f43f5e, tube outline: #e2e8f0.

pedagogical_callouts.title: Continuity in Action
pedagogical_callouts.text: As fluid enters the constricted throat, its cross-sectional area decreases. To maintain constant mass flow rate (A₁v₁ = A₂v₂), the fluid velocity must increase.

pedagogical_callouts.title: Bernoulli's Energy Trade-off
pedagogical_callouts.text: The increase in kinetic energy (½ρv²) in the throat must be balanced by a decrease in pressure energy (P), assuming negligible height change. This causes the pressure drop observed in the manometer tubes.

pedagogical_callouts.title: Venturi Meter Principle
pedagogical_callouts.text: The pressure difference (ΔP) between inlet and throat is proportional to the square of the flow rate. By measuring ΔP, the flow rate can be calculated without moving parts, forming the basis of Venturi flow meters.

pedagogical_callouts.title: Real-World Applications
pedagogical_callouts.text: This principle is used in carburetors (fuel injection), aspirators, medical nebulizers, and industrial flow measurement. The geometry ensures efficient energy conversion with minimal losses compared to abrupt orifices.
